newsitem.title: INDIA: India Ashok Leyland 96/97 1st hlf net up.
newsitem.headline: India Ashok Leyland 96/97 1st hlf net up.

text.p: Indian truck maker Ashok Leyland Ltd said its net profit for the six months ended September 30, 1996, rose to 571 million rupees, from 485 million during the year-ago period.
It said net sales increased to 11.52 billion rupees from 8.28 billion rupees in the year-ago period.

Exports suffered a setback during the six months. The company exported 700 vehicles in the first half of the current year against 1,194 in the year-ago period, it said after a board meeting on Saturday.
The company provided for a tax outgo of 84.6 million rupees in the first half of the current year against nil in the year-ago period, a company spokesman said.
It provided for depreciation of 300.74 million against 231.39 million in the corresponding period of the previous year, he said.
Profit before interest and depreciation rose 78 percent to 993 million from 558 million. Profit before tax, at 656 million, is up 35 percent over the year ago figure, he said.

"The company continues to enjoy firm demand for its diversified range of vehicles and recorded a sale of 20,101 units, an increase of 24 percent against the total industry volume increase of 22 percent," the company said in a statement.
It said the company improved its market share and is on course to notch up a record performance in the current year.
"Ashok Leyland has gone ahead with expansion of the range of their modern cargo trucks by flagging off production of MDV Cargo models at its Hosur factory," it said.
Demand for vehicles continues to be good, but for the potential impact of any slowdown in the economy, it said.
Ashok Leyland is the flagship of the Hinduja Group of companies in India.
